title: Stacked Cubes
statement: A prime power is a number of the form $p^t$, where $p$ is a prime and $t$ is a positive integer. Determine all prime powers that can be written as the sum of the cubes of at least two consecutive positive integers.
hints: The sum of the first $n$ cubes has a simple closed form. Use it to write $a^3+\dots+b^3$ as a difference of two squares, and look at the two factors this gives.

Let $T_n=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$. The sum factorises as $AB$, where $A=T_b-T_{a-1}$ and $B=T_b+T_{a-1}$. If the sum is a power of the prime $p$, then both factors exceed $1$, so $p$ divides both. Argue by divisibility modulo $p$, after writing $A$ and $B$ in terms of $u=a+b$ and $v=b-a+1$.

With $u=a+b$ and $v=b-a+1$, the factors $A=T_b-T_{a-1}$ and $B=T_b+T_{a-1}$ satisfy $uv=2A$ and $4B=u^2+v^2-1$. If $p$ divided both $u$ and $v$, then $4B$ would be $-1$ modulo $p$, which is impossible. Use this and the fact that $u$ and $v$ have opposite parity to show that $v=2$. Then $4B=u^2+3$, and now compare powers of $p$ on the two sides.
solution: Answer. The only such prime power is $9=1^3+2^3$. Suppose $a^3+(a+1)^3+\dots+b^3=p^t$ with $p$ prime, $t\ge1$ and $b>a\ge1$. Let $T_n=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$, so $T_0=0$. Since $1^3+\dots+n^3=T_n^2$, $$p^t=T_b^2-T_{a-1}^2=AB,\qquad A=T_b-T_{a-1},\quad B=T_b+T_{a-1}.$$ Here $A=a+(a+1)+\dots+b\ge 1+2=3$ (this includes $a=1$, where $T_0=0$) and $B\ge A$. So $A$ and $B$ are both powers of $p$ with positive exponent, and $p\mid A$, $p\mid B$. Write $A=p^e$. Put $u=a+b$ and $v=b-a+1\ge2$. Then $u-v=2a-1\ge1$, so $u>v$, and $u+v=2b+1$ is odd, so $u,v$ have opposite parity. $A$ is a sum of $v$ consecutive integers with mean $\frac{u}{2}$, so $uv=2A=2p^e$. Also $$u^2+v^2-1=2a^2+2b^2-2a+2b=2b(b+1)+2a(a-1)=4T_b+4T_{a-1}=4B.$$ If $p\mid u$ and $p\mid v$, then $4B\equiv-1\pmod p$, contradicting $p\mid B$. So $p$ does not divide both $u$ and $v$. Let $w$ be the odd one of $u,v$ and $z$ the even one. Then $w\ge3$ since $u,v\ge2$. As $w$ is an odd divisor of $2p^e$ and $w>1$, $p$ is odd, $w$ is a power of $p$, and $p\mid w$. From $wz=2p^e$ we get $z=2p^s$. If $s\ge1$ then $p$ divides both $u$ and $v$, impossible. So $z=2$. Since $u>v\ge2$, $u\ne2$, so $v=2$ and $u=w=p^e$. Thus $b=a+1$. Now $4B=u^2+3$. Since $p\mid u$ and $p\mid B$, $p\mid 3$, so $p=3$. Then $9\mid u^2$, so $4B=u^2+3\equiv3\pmod 9$, so $9\nmid B$. As $B$ is a power of $3$ with positive exponent, $B=3$. Then $u^2+3=12$, so $u=3$, giving $2a+1=3$, $a=1$, $b=2$. Conversely, $1^3+2^3=9=3^2$ is a prime power and a sum of two consecutive positive cubes. Hence $9$ is the only such prime power.

rubric.criterion: Writes the sum as a product of two integer factors, such as $(T_b-T_{a-1})(T_b+T_{a-1})$ with $T_n=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$, or an equivalent, and shows that both factors exceed $1$, so both are positive powers of $p$. Deduct 1 if the case $a=1$ is mishandled or the bound on the smaller factor is not justified.

Expresses the factors in a pair of variables, such as $uv=2A$ and $4B=u^2+v^2-1$ with $u=a+b$ and $v=b-a+1$, or an equivalent, and proves that $p$ cannot divide both $u$ and $v$, or an equivalent restriction on their common factors. Deduct 1 if the identity for $4B$ is stated correctly but neither derived nor checkable from the working shown.
Deduces that exactly two consecutive cubes are involved, that is, $b=a+1$ (equivalently $v=2$), together with the fact that $p$ is odd. Deduct 1 if the case $p=2$ is missing.

From $b=a+1$, proves that $a=1$ is the only possibility, for example by showing $p=3$ from $4B=u^2+3$ and then comparing powers of $3$, and verifies that $1^3+2^3=9=3^2$ is a prime power. Stating the answer $9$ or checking small cases earns nothing on this line unless $b=a+1$ has been handled in general. Deduct 1 if the verification that $9$ qualifies is missing. A complete proof by another route earns all marks.

Writes the sum as a product of two integer factors $A\le B$, such as $A=T_b-T_{a-1}$ and $B=T_b+T_{a-1}$, and shows that both are positive powers of $p$.
Deduces $A\mid B$ because both are powers of the same prime, and converts this into an equation equivalent to $u^2+v^2-1=2kuv$ with $u=a+b$, $v=b-a+1$ and $k$ a positive integer.
Deduces $\gcd(u,v)=1$ and uses $uv=2p^e$ with $u>v\ge 2$ to conclude that $p$ is odd, $v=2$ and $u=p^e$. Deduct 1 if the case $p=2$ is missing.
Deduces $u\mid v^2-1=3$, so $u=3$, $a=1$ and $b=2$, and verifies that $1^3+2^3=9$ is a prime power.

fatal_errors.error: Treats the two factors of the sum as coprime, or concludes that the smaller factor equals $1$, when both are in fact positive powers of $p$ and so share the factor $p$.
Assumes without proof that the sum has exactly two terms, or considers only a limited number of terms, so that the general case $b>a+1$ is never excluded.
Infers the answer from a numerical check of small cases or an observed pattern, with no general argument.
